newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIA REASSURES OVER NUCLEAR PLANT.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIA REASSURES OVER NUCLEAR PLANT.

text.p: Lithuania on Thursday pledged to follow the recommendations of an international panel and implement crucial safety measures at its Ignalina nuclear plant.
Ignalina has the largest Chernobyl-type RBMK reactors, responsible in 1986 for the world's worst nuclear disaster.
An international panel in London two weeks' ago said both of the plant's reactors, shut every year at different times for maintenance, not be reactivated until safety upgrades are made.
One of the units, unit 2, is currently shut down for its routine maintenance.

"I can assure you the unit 2 reactor will not be brought back on line until safety measures are implemented," Lithuanian Foreign Minister Algirdas Saudargas said at a news conference with visiting European Union Commissioner Hans van den Broek.

Ignalina, which provides as much as 90 percent of Lithuania's electricity, has been the sight of several worrying incidents such as a fire in a turbine room and two cranes becoming entangled when replacing nuclear fuel rods.
"We think things should be moving a little faster in Lithuania when it comes to nuclear safety," said Jan Nistad, the director of the Swedish International Project on Nuclear Safety.
"These recommendations were made to put pressure on the government. Lithuania needs the reactor unit operating next winter and we know that," he said.

Uner the terms of a 33 million ECU agreement with the G-7 and the European Bank for reconstruction and Development (EBRD), the plant is slated for closure in 10 to 15 years when its reactor channels need to be replaced.
